title: Agentic AI: 35-Day Daily Learning Plan
planning_note: Five consecutive 7-day blocks. Days 1–6 of each week focus on learning/building; day 7 is used for integration, review, tests, and catch-up. Daily time is a target, not a guarantee of mastery.
provider_strategy: Choose one LLM provider SDK for the first two weeks (for example, Google GenAI or OpenAI). Keep provider-specific calls behind a small adapter. Do not learn multiple SDKs simultaneously.

days.title: LLM foundations and first API call
days.learning_objective: Understand the request/response lifecycle between a Python application and a hosted language model.
hands_on_tasks: Create the project repository and virtual environment.
Store the model API key in an environment variable and load it without hard-coding secrets.
Call one model through one provider SDK and print the response.
Record model name, request latency, and basic usage metadata when the provider returns it.
days.deliverable: A working Python LLM client with a .env.example file and a README setup section.
acceptance_criteria: The API key is not committed to source control.
A valid request returns a response.
Missing credentials produce a clear, safe error.

days.title: Structured outputs and Pydantic
days.learning_objective: Make model responses machine-readable and validate them before application code uses them.
hands_on_tasks: Define Pydantic models for an agent decision and a final answer.
Request structured output using the provider-supported schema feature, or request JSON and validate it locally if strict structured output is unavailable.
Test valid output, missing fields, wrong types, and extra fields.
Return validation errors to the application without treating model text as trusted data.
days.deliverable: A validated decision schema and a small test suite covering valid and invalid model output.
acceptance_criteria: Application logic consumes validated Pydantic objects, not unvalidated JSON strings.
Invalid output is rejected and logged safely.

days.title: Tool definitions and function calling
days.learning_objective: Understand how a model requests a tool call and how application code makes the tool available.
concepts: Tool names, descriptions and JSON arguments
Separation of model decision and Python execution
hands_on_tasks: Write two safe Python tools, such as calculator and read_project_notes.
Describe each tool with an explicit argument schema.
Send tool definitions to the model using the chosen provider SDK.
Inspect the returned tool-call request; do not execute arbitrary model-generated code.
days.deliverable: A small tool registry containing two typed, documented tools.
acceptance_criteria: Tool arguments are validated before execution.
The model can request a tool, but only the Python application executes it.
Unknown tool names are rejected.

days.title: Tool dispatcher and observation cycle
days.learning_objective: Implement the application-side mechanics for dispatching tool calls and returning results to the model.
hands_on_tasks: Implement a dispatcher mapping approved tool names to Python functions.
Execute a requested tool and capture success or failure as a structured result.
Append the tool result to the provider conversation format.
Test unknown tools, invalid arguments, tool exceptions, and large outputs.
days.deliverable: A reusable dispatcher that executes approved functions and returns structured observations.
acceptance_criteria: Only registered tools can run.
Tool exceptions do not crash the whole process.
Tool output is bounded and serializable.

days.title: ReAct-style agent loop and stopping rules
days.learning_objective: Build a bounded reasoning-and-action control loop without exposing private chain-of-thought.
concepts: Why visible progress summaries differ from hidden reasoning
hands_on_tasks: Implement a loop that sends the current conversation to the model.
When the model requests a tool, validate and execute it, then continue with the observation.
Stop when the model returns a final response or a budget is reached.
Emit user-safe progress events such as tool_started and tool_completed, not hidden internal reasoning.
days.deliverable: A bounded single-agent loop that can call multiple tools and terminate safely.
acceptance_criteria: The loop has a maximum-iteration limit and timeout.
It terminates on a final response.
It stops safely when the budget is exceeded.

days.title: Build the zero-framework CLI coding assistant
days.learning_objective: Combine the raw LLM, schemas, tools, dispatcher, and loop into a useful command-line agent.
concepts: Error observation and bounded repair cycle
hands_on_tasks: Create read_file and write_file tools restricted to a dedicated workspace directory.
Create run_tests that runs only a fixed, allowlisted test command in that workspace.
Ask the agent to inspect a small sample project, make a fix, and rerun tests.
Require confirmation before overwriting important files; never expose unrestricted shell access.
days.deliverable: Project 1: a CLI coding assistant that can inspect files, make bounded edits, and run an allowlisted test command.
acceptance_criteria: Path traversal outside the workspace is blocked.
Only allowlisted commands can run.
The agent stops after a configured attempt limit.
All file changes are reviewable.

days.title: Week 1 review and integration tests
days.learning_objective: Consolidate the raw agent mechanics and document what the application—not the model—controls.
hands_on_tasks: Run the CLI assistant against at least three tasks, including one that should fail.
Test invalid arguments, unknown tools, tool exceptions, and iteration exhaustion.
Review logs and remove secrets or sensitive file contents.
Write an architecture note explaining the control loop.
days.deliverable: A tested Week 1 project with setup instructions, architecture notes, and known limitations.
acceptance_criteria: The happy path and failure paths are tested.
The agent cannot escape its workspace or run arbitrary commands.
The README explains how to configure and run the project.

days.title: Agent state and short-term memory
days.learning_objective: Distinguish conversation history, execution state, and persistent memory.
hands_on_tasks: Define a typed AgentState model containing messages, task metadata, and tool observations.
Keep only the relevant recent context and summarize older interaction when needed.
Add tests proving that execution state and user preferences are stored separately.
Set a maximum history size.
days.deliverable: A bounded short-term state manager for conversations and in-progress tasks.
acceptance_criteria: State has a documented schema.
Old history is handled under a defined policy.
User memory is not confused with transient tool results.

days.title: Embeddings and document preparation
days.learning_objective: Prepare text for semantic retrieval and understand the limits of embedding similarity.
hands_on_tasks: Load a small set of Markdown or text documents.
Split documents into chunks with source and section metadata.
Generate embeddings using one embedding model.
Compare chunk sizes on a few example queries and inspect poor matches.
days.deliverable: A repeatable document-ingestion script that creates chunks, metadata, and embeddings.
acceptance_criteria: Each chunk retains a stable source reference.
The same embedding model is used for indexing and querying.
Empty or malformed documents are handled.

days.title: Vector storage with PostgreSQL and pgvector
days.learning_objective: Store embeddings and retrieve semantically similar chunks from a vector database.
hands_on_tasks: Create a PostgreSQL database with pgvector enabled.
Create a documents/chunks table with source metadata and an embedding column.
Insert sample chunks and query nearest neighbors.
Add a metadata filter and test empty-result behavior.
days.deliverable: A PostgreSQL-backed vector store with an ingestion and similarity-search path.
acceptance_criteria: Vectors can be inserted and queried.
Returned chunks include source metadata.
Database credentials are environment-configured.

days.title: Basic RAG pipeline and grounded answers
days.learning_objective: Build retrieval-augmented generation with source-aware answer formatting.
hands_on_tasks: Embed a user question and retrieve relevant chunks.
Pass retrieved passages and source identifiers to the model.
Require the answer to cite the supplied source identifiers.
Return an explicit insufficient-evidence response when retrieval is empty or weak.
days.deliverable: A document question-answering service that returns answers with traceable source references.
acceptance_criteria: Every factual answer cites retrieved source IDs.
No-source questions trigger abstention or a clarification.
Retrieval and generation are separately testable.

days.title: Retrieval quality and relevance evaluation
days.learning_objective: Measure whether retrieved chunks are useful before trusting generated answers.
hands_on_tasks: Create a small set of questions with expected source documents.
Score retrieved chunks using a structured relevance rubric or a separate grader.
Compare top-k results for several chunking configurations.
Record misses and false positives.
days.deliverable: A small retrieval evaluation dataset and a report showing retrieval failure cases.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation queries have expected source references.
Retrieval results can be inspected and scored.
The report identifies at least three improvement opportunities.

days.title: Agentic retrieval and CRAG-inspired correction
days.learning_objective: Let the agent decide whether retrieval is sufficient, reformulate a query, or use a fallback source.
hands_on_tasks: Create a retrieval-grader schema with relevant, partially_relevant, and insufficient outcomes.
If results are insufficient, rewrite the search query and retry a limited number of times.
Add an optional external search adapter behind an interface; use a mock in tests.
Require the final response to distinguish internal documents from external sources.
days.deliverable: An agentic retrieval flow with relevance grading, bounded query rewriting, and a testable fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Retries are bounded.
External search is called only under the defined fallback condition.
Sources are labeled by origin.

days.title: Long-term memory and Week 2 integration
days.learning_objective: Persist selected facts across sessions without storing every conversation indiscriminately.
hands_on_tasks: Persist explicitly selected preferences or project facts in PostgreSQL.
Retrieve relevant memories for a new session.
Add update/delete operations and a retention policy.
Integrate short-term state, document RAG, and long-term memory in Project 2.
days.deliverable: Project 2: an agentic research assistant with document retrieval, retrieval correction, citations, and opt-in persistent memory.
acceptance_criteria: Memory is scoped to the correct user or test profile.
Users can inspect and delete stored memories.
The agent does not treat retrieved memory as trusted instructions.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: LangGraph state, nodes, and edges
days.learning_objective: Translate a manually implemented agent loop into a state graph.
hands_on_tasks: Install LangGraph in a separate project environment.
Define a typed workflow state.
Create nodes for planning, retrieval, and response generation.
Connect nodes and run a basic acyclic workflow before adding loops.
days.deliverable: A small LangGraph workflow with explicit state and independently testable nodes.
acceptance_criteria: State transitions are visible and deterministic where possible.
Each node has a clear input/output contract.
A simple workflow runs end to end.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: Conditional edges and cyclic workflows
days.learning_objective: Model branching, tool execution, retries, and completion as graph transitions.
hands_on_tasks: Add a route that chooses between retrieval, a tool, or a final answer.
Add a bounded retry edge for insufficient retrieval.
Add an error-handling node and an explicit terminal state.
Test each branch with controlled fixtures.
days.deliverable: A cyclic LangGraph workflow with tested conditional routing and terminal conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Every possible route has a defined outcome.
Cycles have a bounded exit condition.
Errors do not silently disappear.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: Checkpointing and persistent graph state
days.learning_objective: Persist graph execution state so an in-progress thread can be resumed.
hands_on_tasks: Configure a supported LangGraph checkpointer for development.
Run a workflow, stop it, and resume using the same thread identifier.
Inspect which state is persisted and which secrets must not be persisted.
Write a restart/resume test.
days.deliverable: A checkpointed workflow that can resume an interrupted thread.
acceptance_criteria: A resumed thread restores expected state.
Thread IDs isolate separate conversations.
Secrets are excluded from persisted state.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: Interrupts and human approval
days.learning_objective: Pause a workflow at a controlled point and resume it after an explicit human decision.
hands_on_tasks: Add an approval checkpoint before a mock publishing action.
Pause with a structured approval request.
Resume with approve and reject decisions.
Test restart between pause and resume and reject stale or mismatched approval IDs.
days.deliverable: A workflow that pauses for approval and resumes on an explicit decision.
acceptance_criteria: No publishing action occurs before approval.
Rejecting approval terminates or reroutes the workflow.
Approval decisions are auditable.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: Multi-agent patterns and supervisor design
days.learning_objective: Understand when specialized agents help and how a supervisor coordinates them.
hands_on_tasks: Define researcher, fact-checker, and writer responsibilities.
Create a supervisor routing decision with typed outputs.
Use bounded handoffs and a shared task state.
Compare a multi-agent design with a simpler single-agent workflow.
days.deliverable: A documented multi-agent design with clear role boundaries and a supervisor route.
acceptance_criteria: Each specialist has a narrow responsibility.
The supervisor can stop or request another step.
The design explains why multiple agents are justified.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: MCP server and client fundamentals
days.learning_objective: Connect tools through the Model Context Protocol rather than custom one-off integrations.
concepts: MCP host, client, and server roles
hands_on_tasks: Read the current MCP Python SDK documentation for the installed SDK release.
Build a local MCP server exposing one read-only project search tool.
Connect to it with a small MCP client.
Validate inputs and document server permissions and transport settings.
days.deliverable: A local MCP server and client that exchange a validated tool request and result.
acceptance_criteria: The client discovers and calls the intended tool.
The server exposes only explicitly registered capabilities.
Transport and permissions are documented.

days.phase: State Graphs, MCP, and Multi-Agent Orchestration
days.title: Integrate LangGraph, MCP, and specialist agents
days.learning_objective: Combine graph orchestration with MCP-backed tools in a complete research workflow.
hands_on_tasks: Connect the researcher to an MCP search tool.
Connect the fact-checker to source retrieval/verification tools.
Route unsupported claims back to research with a retry limit.
Generate a cited report and run end-to-end tests.
days.deliverable: Project 3: a LangGraph research workflow using MCP tools and specialist roles.
acceptance_criteria: The graph can research, verify, and write a report.
Unsupported claims trigger a bounded correction path.
Tool permissions and error paths are tested.

days.title: Authorization and human control boundaries
days.learning_objective: Define who can request, approve, and execute consequential agent actions.
hands_on_tasks: Define read-only, draft, and publish permission levels.
Enforce authorization in Python tool handlers, not only in prompts.
Bind approval decisions to an authenticated approver and a specific action payload.
Add audit events for denied and approved actions.
days.deliverable: A permission layer that separates agent intent from authorization to execute actions.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthorized tool calls are denied server-side.
Approval is bound to the exact pending action.
Authorization outcomes are logged.

days.title: Budgets, timeouts, retries, and cancellation
days.learning_objective: Prevent runaway loops and control resource use across model and tool calls.
hands_on_tasks: Add max-step, wall-clock, and tool-call budgets.
Add timeouts and bounded retries for transient tool failures.
Use idempotency keys where retries could repeat a side effect.
Test cancellation and budget exhaustion.
days.deliverable: A reusable execution policy applied to all agent runs and tools.
acceptance_criteria: Runs stop when configured budgets are reached.
Transient failures retry only within limits.
Side-effecting calls are protected against accidental duplication.

days.title: Input/output validation and safe error recovery
days.learning_objective: Recover from malformed model output and tool failures without trusting arbitrary generated instructions.
hands_on_tasks: Validate every tool argument and important model output.
Return compact, redacted error summaries to the model when a retry is allowed.
Keep full diagnostics in protected logs, not in user-visible output.
Add fallback or human escalation for non-recoverable errors.
days.deliverable: A validation and error-recovery layer with safe, structured failure handling.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid inputs never reach sensitive tools.
Secrets and private data are redacted from model feedback.
Repeated failures end in a clear failure state or human escalation.

days.title: Prompt injection and tool security
days.learning_objective: Protect agent workflows from malicious instructions in user input and retrieved content.
hands_on_tasks: Add adversarial test documents containing instructions that conflict with system policy.
Mark retrieved content as untrusted data and keep tool policy in application code.
Restrict file, network, and database tool capabilities.
Test attempts to reveal secrets or trigger unauthorized actions.
days.deliverable: A prompt-injection test suite and a set of enforced tool security controls.
acceptance_criteria: Retrieved text cannot change server-side permissions.
Secrets are not available to the model unless explicitly needed.
Unauthorized or out-of-scope actions are blocked.

days.title: Idempotency, auditability, and fallbacks
days.learning_objective: Make side-effecting operations safe to retry and easier to investigate.
hands_on_tasks: Create an action record before executing a mock publish operation.
Use a stable idempotency key to prevent duplicate execution.
Record actor, requested action, approval, result, and timestamps.
Simulate a timeout after an action succeeds and verify a retry does not duplicate it.
days.deliverable: An auditable mock publishing tool with duplicate-execution protection.
acceptance_criteria: A repeated request with the same idempotency key does not repeat the side effect.
Action status can be reconciled after a timeout.
Audit records identify the decision and outcome.

days.title: Agent evaluation and failure simulation
days.learning_objective: Evaluate both final answers and the sequence of actions taken to produce them.
hands_on_tasks: Create test cases for success, ambiguity, tool failure, prompt injection, and approval rejection.
Score task completion, source support, policy compliance, and tool-use correctness.
Compare expected tool behavior with recorded traces.
Run a regression suite after changing prompts or tools.
days.deliverable: A repeatable agent evaluation suite with a documented scoring rubric.
acceptance_criteria: The dataset includes normal and adversarial cases.
Scores are reproducible for a fixed model/configuration where possible.
Failures include trace IDs and actionable diagnoses.

days.title: Integrate the guarded publishing pipeline
days.learning_objective: Harden the research workflow with authorization, checkpoints, budgets, and evaluations.
hands_on_tasks: Integrate the researcher, fact checker, writer, and mock publisher.
Add approval interrupts, role checks, timeouts, idempotency, and audit events.
Run the evaluation suite and fix critical failures.
Document the safe operating procedure and known limitations.
days.deliverable: Project 4: a guarded research-and-publishing pipeline that requires approval before publishing.
acceptance_criteria: Publishing is impossible without valid approval.
Prompt injection and duplicate-action tests pass.
The workflow can resume after a pause or process restart.

days.title: FastAPI service design for agents
days.learning_objective: Expose agent runs through a backend API with validated requests and explicit run lifecycle.
concepts: FastAPI routes and Pydantic request/response models
hands_on_tasks: Create endpoints to submit a task, retrieve run status, and fetch a completed result.
Validate request size and parameters.
Return a stable run ID and explicit lifecycle states.
Keep provider and orchestration code outside route handlers.
days.deliverable: A FastAPI service that starts agent runs and exposes status and results.
acceptance_criteria: API contracts are validated.
Long-running work does not block the request handler.
Run ownership and authorization are checked.

days.title: Async execution and progress streaming
days.learning_objective: Deliver useful execution progress to a frontend without exposing private internal reasoning.
concepts: Async tool calls and sync boundaries
hands_on_tasks: Implement an SSE endpoint for run events.
Emit events such as agent_started, tool_started, tool_completed, approval_required, and agent_completed.
Do not stream hidden chain-of-thought; provide concise status summaries only.
Test disconnect and reconnect behavior.
days.deliverable: A streaming endpoint that emits structured, user-safe progress events.
acceptance_criteria: Events are ordered and include run IDs.
No hidden reasoning or secrets are streamed.
A client can recover final status after reconnecting.

days.title: Persistence and resumable production runs
days.learning_objective: Persist conversations, workflow state, and action records with clear ownership and retention.
hands_on_tasks: Persist run metadata, user/session ownership, approval status, and final result.
Configure durable graph checkpointing using the selected supported backend.
Create migrations and test recovery after process restart.
Define retention and cleanup for old runs.
days.deliverable: A durable persistence layer for agent runs and resumable workflow state.
acceptance_criteria: Runs survive application restart.
User/session boundaries are enforced.
Schema changes are managed through migrations.

days.title: Tracing and observability
days.learning_objective: Inspect model calls, tool calls, latency, errors, and run costs across agent workflows.
hands_on_tasks: Integrate one tracing platform, choosing Langfuse or Arize Phoenix.
Trace each run and its model/tool spans.
Record latency, outcome, and token/cost metadata when available.
Redact secrets and sensitive content before export.
days.deliverable: A traceable agent service with correlated model and tool spans.
acceptance_criteria: A run can be inspected end to end.
Errors and latency can be attributed to a step.
Sensitive fields are filtered from telemetry.

days.title: Docker and deployment readiness
days.learning_objective: Package the service reproducibly and prepare a safe deployment configuration.
hands_on_tasks: Create a Docker image for the FastAPI service.
Keep secrets outside the image and source repository.
Add health/readiness endpoints and structured logs.
Run the container locally with a production-like environment configuration.
days.deliverable: A containerized service with documented configuration and health checks.
acceptance_criteria: The image builds from a clean checkout.
Secrets are injected at runtime.
Health checks reflect service readiness.

days.title: Production evaluation, load, and cost review
days.learning_objective: Measure whether the deployed agent is reliable, responsive, and affordable enough for its intended workload.
hands_on_tasks: Run the evaluation dataset against the deployed service.
Measure success rate, failure rate, latency, and cost per completed task.
Test moderate concurrency and provider/tool rate limits.
Define release thresholds and a rollback procedure.
days.deliverable: A production-readiness report with evaluation, latency, cost, and known-risk metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics are measured rather than guessed.
Release thresholds are explicit.
Critical regression failures block release.

days.title: Final capstone review and demo
days.learning_objective: Demonstrate the complete agentic system and explain its architecture, safety, and operational behavior.
hands_on_tasks: Demonstrate research, source verification, approval pause/resume, and mock or controlled publishing.
Show a trace for a successful run and a failed run.
Present evaluation results, limitations, and cost/latency measurements.
Tag a release and publish setup, architecture, and operations documentation.
days.deliverable: Project 5: a production-oriented Agentic Research & Publishing API with evaluation and observability.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh setup can run using documented steps.
Approval and authorization gates work.
Evaluation and tracing evidence are included.
The demo clearly states what is mocked and what is connected to live services.
